questions.q: Why does this capstone run one final validation pass across all four pieces together, instead of relying on each piece's own individual checks?
options: Because the individual checks were never actually performed
Because a program built in pieces can have a seam between pieces that no individual check catches, visible only when all pieces are checked together at the same moment
Because Howard Okonjo requires it as a formality with no real purpose
Because the risk register automatically fails without it
questions.explain: Each piece can report healthy on its own while still disagreeing with another piece right now — only a simultaneous, combined check can surface that kind of gap.

questions.q: What does this final pass specifically check about the risk register?
options: That the register has never been edited since it was first created
That GRC-RISK-0147 shows status Closed with all four corrective actions complete, and that no new open item from this phase is sitting without an owner or due date
That the register contains at least 100 entries
That the register has been deleted now that the incident is resolved
questions.explain: The register check confirms the specific finding is fully closed out and that nothing new from this phase was left unowned or undated.

questions.q: What is a 'seam,' as this lesson defines it?
options: A physical boundary between two OT segments
A gap that exists only between two individually correct components, invisible to either one checked alone
A synonym for a stale break-glass grant
A formatting style used in the risk register
questions.explain: A seam is specifically the kind of gap that only shows up when two systems' current states are compared at the same moment, not a flaw in either system by itself.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between this final pass and Lesson 24's validation gate?
options: They are unrelated; the validation gate was discarded once the second segment shipped
This final pass applies the identical standard — don't trust a single point-in-time report, confirm agreement across checks — one level up, to the entire capstone instead of one rollout
This final pass replaces the need for Lesson 24's validation gate retroactively
The validation gate only applied to Lesson 20's board presentation
questions.explain: Both apply the same discipline — refusing to declare something validated until independent evidence agrees — just at different scales.

questions.q: According to this lesson's checklist, when is the program actually considered validated?
options: As soon as the automation's dashboard shows 'all clear' on its most recent run
Only when every checklist item — segmentation, identity, automation, and the risk register — reads complete, confirmed together in the same pass, not based on each one's last separate check
As soon as the board approves the budget in Lesson 20
Once Priya Nair personally signs off on the rollout
questions.explain: The whole point of the final pass is simultaneity — every piece has to agree right now, together, not just have looked fine individually at some earlier point.
